_about.what: Ankle, foot & balance — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling" }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place.
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken; "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

sources.name: Achilles Foot & Ankle Center — ankle injury rehabilitation exercises
Evolve NY — foot and ankle strengthening

moves.name: Wall calf stretch
moves.summary: Gastrocnemius (straight knee) or soleus (bent knee) stretch, verified heel-down and knee-correct.
moves.setup: Stand facing a wall with both hands on it, side-on to the camera at hip height, 2–3 m away. Step the stretching leg back so it is the leg nearest the camera; toes pointing at the wall. Whole body from hands to back heel in frame.
moves.why: Side-on, the three things that make or break the stretch — back heel on the floor, back knee straight or bent, shin leaning toward the wall — are each a direct height or angle read.

guide.surface: Wall or doorframe. Barefoot or in flat shoes. Non-slip floor.

points.t: Both palms flat on the wall at shoulder height, shoulder-width apart, arms nearly straight with a soft elbow.
Lean by bending the elbows slightly and moving the hips toward the wall — the arms guide, they do not push.
Stepped straight back, toes pointing directly at the wall — not turned out. Heel flat on the floor and pressed down throughout.
Foot in line with its hip, not crossed behind the body; hip-width from the front foot.
Straight-knee (calf) variant: back knee fully straight. Bent-knee (soleus) variant: back knee softly bent 20–40°, heel still down.
Front foot flat, toes at the wall, about 30 cm from it. Front knee bends as you lean and stays over the front foot, not past it.
Hips square to the wall, both hip bones the same distance from it. Move the hips forward as one unit; do not push one side forward.
Lean from the ankle, not by folding at the waist — shoulders, hips and back ankle form one straight line.
Spine long and neutral, chest up, shoulders down and relaxed.
Eyes on the wall in front of you, chin level.

Ease in until you feel a firm pull in the calf (straight knee) or lower toward the Achilles (bent knee), never pain. Breathe slowly; on each breath out, see if the hips can come a little further forward.
Hold 20–60 s, 2–3 times per side, ideally after a warm-up or at the end of a walk.

guide.stop: Sharp pain in the Achilles or the arch, or if the heel cannot stay down without pain — shorten the step instead.

moves.enterCue: Hands on the wall, step the back leg back, and lean in
moves.tempo: Ease in over 3 s, hold, breathe.
moves.dosage: 3 × 30 s each leg, once or twice a day.
moves.progression: Step the back foot further away; the bent-knee variant for the soleus.
moves.regression: Step closer to the wall; hands higher.
moves.contraindications: Sharp calf or Achilles pain, or a recent calf tear.

faults.label: Back heel lifting
faults.tip: The stretch only reaches the calf when the heel stays flat. Step the foot closer to the wall if it will not stay down.

faults.label: Back knee bending
faults.tip: For the calf (gastrocnemius) stretch the back knee must stay straight; a bent knee shifts the stretch to the soleus.

faults.label: Back knee not bent enough
faults.cue: Bend the back knee a little more
faults.tip: For the soleus variant keep the back knee softly bent, about 20–40°.

faults.label: Not leaning in enough
faults.cue: Lean in until you feel the calf
faults.tip: Move the hips toward the wall; the shin should tilt forward at least 10–15°.

faults.label: Hands not at shoulder height
faults.cue: Hands on the wall at shoulder height
faults.tip: Hands too high pull the shoulders up and arch the back; too low folds you at the waist.

faults.label: Hands too low on the wall
faults.tip: Hands too high pull the shoulders up and arch the back; too low folds you at the waist.

faults.label: Front knee straight
faults.cue: Bend the front knee as you lean
faults.tip: The front knee bends toward the wall so the hips can travel forward; a straight front leg blocks the lean.

faults.label: Bending at the hips
faults.cue: Keep your body in a straight line
faults.tip: Lean from the ankle, not the waist — shoulders, hips and back knee in one line.

moves.name: Calf raise (both legs)
moves.summary: Rise onto the balls of both feet, pause at the top, lower slowly with the knees straight.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, fingertips on a wall, feet hip-width. Push up onto the balls of the feet as high as you can, pause, then lower over three seconds.
moves.why: From the side the ankle angle opens as the heel rises, which counts the reps, and a knee bending to help is visible as the hip–knee–ankle angle dropping.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, hold 1 s, down 3 s.
moves.progression: Single leg; heels off a step for extra range.
moves.contraindications: Achilles pain that worsens through the set.

faults.label: Knees bending to help
faults.tip: Lock the knees so the calf does the lifting; bent knees shift the work and shorten the range.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Rolling onto the outside of the feet
faults.tip: Press through the big toe joint at the top so the ankle rises straight rather than rolling out.

faults.label: Not reaching full height
faults.cue: All the way up on your toes
faults.tip: The last centimetre at the top is where the calf works hardest. Rise until the heels are high.

faults.label: Dropping the heels
faults.tip: The controlled lowering is what builds and rehabilitates the Achilles.

faults.label: Leaning on the support
faults.tip: Pushing down through the hands takes body weight off the calves.

guide.surface: Firm floor; a wall or rail in front.
guide.stop: Achilles or arch pain that builds.
guide.cannotSee: The foot rolling outward — that is a front-view detail.

points.t: Rise as high as possible; lower slowly.
Weight over the big toe at the top.
Straight throughout.

moves.name: Single-leg calf raise
moves.summary: A calf raise on one leg — the standard for Achilles and ankle rehab.
moves.setup: Stand on one leg side-on to the phone, working leg nearest, fingertips on a wall. Rise onto the ball of the foot, pause, lower over three seconds. Keep the knee straight and the ankle from rolling out.
moves.why: The ankle angle counts each rise from the side; the knee bending shows as the leg angle closing.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, hold 1 s, down 3 s.
moves.progression: Heel off a step; hold a weight.
moves.contraindications: Achilles pain above a mild ache.

faults.label: Knee bending to help
faults.tip: Keep the knee locked; the rise comes from the ankle alone.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Ankle rolling outward
faults.tip: Drive through the big toe joint so the heel rises straight up.

faults.label: Not reaching full height
faults.cue: All the way up on your toes
faults.tip: Full height every rep; when you cannot, the set is finished.

faults.label: Dropping the heel
faults.tip: Control on the way down is the part that rebuilds an Achilles tendon.

guide.stop: Achilles pain, or the ankle rolling painfully.

points.t: Full rise, slow lower, heel tracking straight up.
Straight and still.

moves.name: Tibialis raise
moves.summary: Back against a wall, feet a step out, lift the toes and forefoot off the floor with the heels down.
moves.setup: Lean your back on a wall with the feet 30–40 cm in front of it, side-on to the phone. Keeping the heels down, lift the toes and balls of both feet as high as you can, then lower.
moves.why: The ankle angle closing as the toes rise counts each rep from the side. The movement is small, so only the count is trusted.
moves.tempo: Up 1 s, hold 1 s, down 2 s.
moves.progression: Feet further from the wall; single leg.
moves.contraindications: Shin pain that persists after the set.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.tip: The heels stay down; if they lift you are rocking, not lifting the toes.

faults.label: Bouncing the reps
faults.tip: Hold the toes up for a second on every rep.

faults.label: Curling the toes
faults.tip: Curling the toes upward is a smaller muscle. Bring the whole forefoot up as a block.

faults.label: Sliding down the wall
faults.tip: Sliding down turns it into a squat and takes the shin out of the movement.

guide.surface: A wall and a floor with grip.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the heels stay fully planted.

points.t: Toes and forefoot lift; heels stay down.
Back resting on the wall, body straight.

moves.name: Ankle alphabet
moves.summary: Sitting with the leg supported, draw the letters of the alphabet in the air with the big toe.
moves.setup: Sit with the leg out and the foot clear of the floor. Move only the ankle and draw each letter A to Z as large as the ankle allows.
moves.why: The foot traces small shapes in every direction; a single camera cannot follow them. Follow the guide and log the set.
moves.contraindications: Sharp ankle pain in any direction — stop and note which.

faults.label: Moving the knee instead of the ankle
faults.tip: Rest the thigh so the shin stays still; the ankle draws the letters.

faults.label: Pushing through a sharp catch
faults.tip: A stretch is fine; a sharp catch in one direction is worth telling your physio about.

faults.label: Letters too small
faults.tip: Reach the end of the range in every direction; the point is motion, not speed.

faults.label: Rushing the letters
faults.tip: Speed hides the stiff directions. Slow enough to notice where it catches.

guide.surface: A chair or the floor with the leg supported.
guide.cannotSee: Any of it — the foot moves in all directions at once.

points.t: Draws each letter to the end of the range.
Still — supported by the chair.

moves.name: Towel curl
moves.summary: Sitting, scrunch a towel toward you with the toes, heel staying on the floor.
moves.setup: Sit with a towel flat on the floor under the foot. Keeping the heel down, curl the toes to draw the towel toward you, release, repeat until it is bunched up.
moves.why: The toes move a few millimetres under a towel; there is nothing a phone can count. Follow the guide and log the set.
moves.progression: A small weight on the far end of the towel.
moves.contraindications: Cramp in the arch that does not ease.

faults.label: Heel lifting
faults.tip: The heel stays planted so the toes, not the ankle, pull the towel.

faults.label: Clawing with the tips of the toes
faults.cue: Flat toes — pull with the arch
faults.tip: Spread the toes and pull with the whole pad, not the tips.

faults.label: Curling with the toe tips
faults.tip: The arch should do the pulling. Clawing with the toe tips can aggravate the top of the foot.

faults.label: Lifting the foot to reset
faults.tip: Lifting the whole foot to grab more towel uses the shin instead of the arch.

guide.surface: Smooth floor so the towel slides.
guide.stop: Arch cramp that does not settle.

points.t: Heel planted; toes spread and pull the towel.

moves.name: Banded dorsiflexion
moves.summary: Band around the top of the foot anchored in front; pull the toes up toward the shin.
moves.setup: Sit on the floor with the leg out, side-on to the phone, band looped over the top of the foot and anchored ahead of you. Pull the toes toward you against the band, pause, release slowly.
moves.why: The ankle angle closing as the toes pull up counts each rep from the side; the range is small, so only the count is trusted.
moves.tempo: Pull 1 s, hold 1 s, release 2 s.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Bending the knee to help
faults.tip: Keep the knee straight so the shin muscle does the pulling.

faults.label: Letting the band snap back
faults.tip: The return is half the work — two seconds out.

faults.label: Leading with the toes
faults.tip: Pull the foot up as one piece; toe-only movement misses the tibialis anterior.

faults.label: Rolling the foot inward
faults.tip: Rolling in swaps the target for a different muscle. Keep the little toe and big toe level.

guide.surface: Floor; the anchor must not move.
guide.cannotSee: The foot turning in or out as it pulls.

points.t: Toes pull straight toward the shin against the band.
Straight, thigh resting.

moves.name: Banded eversion & inversion
moves.summary: Sitting, turn the sole of the foot outward then inward against a band.
moves.setup: Sit with the legs out, band looped around the forefoot and anchored to the side. Keeping the knee still, turn the sole outward against the band (eversion), release; then re-anchor the other way and turn it inward (inversion).
moves.why: The foot rotates about the shin — a movement a phone sees as almost nothing from any angle. Follow the guide and log each direction.
moves.tempo: Turn 1 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s.
moves.contraindications: Pain on the outside of the ankle after a sprain that has not been assessed.

faults.label: Rotating the whole leg
faults.tip: Hold the shin with a hand if needed; only the foot turns.

faults.label: Turning the whole leg
faults.tip: If the thigh rolls, the hip is doing it. Pin the knee and turn only below the ankle.

faults.label: Tiny movements
faults.cue: Turn the foot all the way
faults.tip: Take the sole as far out (or in) as it goes each rep.

faults.label: Letting the band snap back
faults.tip: The slow return is the half most people skip, and the half the ankle needs.

guide.surface: Floor or a chair; band anchored to a table leg.
guide.stop: Sharp pain on the outside or inside of the ankle.
guide.cannotSee: The foot turning — the movement is a rotation the phone cannot resolve.

points.t: Turns fully against the band; knee and shin stay still.

moves.name: Single-leg balance
moves.summary: Stand on one leg, hips level, and hold still.
moves.setup: Face the phone, lift one foot a few centimetres, soft standing knee, hands free. Keep the hips level and the trunk still. Hold.
moves.why: Facing the phone shows the trunk swaying and the pelvis dropping, so the timer runs only while you are steady. Whether the other foot is really off the floor is not checked.
moves.progression: Eyes closed; stand on a cushion; turn the head side to side.
moves.regression: Fingertip on a wall; shorter holds.
moves.contraindications: Dizziness; falls risk without something to hold.

faults.label: Free-side hip dropping
faults.tip: Lift the free hip slightly; the standing hip muscles hold the pelvis level.

faults.label: Locking the standing knee
faults.tip: A slightly bent knee lets the ankle and hip do the balancing.

faults.label: Gripping with the toes
faults.tip: Clawing the toes is a sign of a wobbling ankle. Spread them and let the whole foot work.

faults.label: Eyes darting around
faults.cue: Fix your eyes on one spot
faults.tip: A steady gaze steadies the balance. Progress by closing the eyes once 30 s is easy.

guide.surface: Firm floor; a wall within reach.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the lifted foot is really off the floor.

points.t: Level throughout the hold.
Upright and still; no swaying.
Soft knee, foot gripping the floor.

moves.name: Tandem stance
moves.summary: Heel to toe on a line, hold still without stepping.
moves.setup: Face the phone and place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toes. Hands free, look ahead. Hold, then swap feet.
moves.why: Facing the phone shows the trunk swaying and the pelvis tilting, so the timer runs only while you are steady.
moves.progression: Eyes closed; walk heel to toe along a line.
moves.regression: Feet slightly apart; fingertip on a wall.

faults.label: Stepping out
faults.tip: If you step, restart the hold — do not count the time before it.

faults.label: Waving the arms
faults.tip: Use the ankles and hips to balance; keep the hands relaxed at the sides.

faults.label: Feet not in line
faults.tip: A gap between the feet makes it a normal stance. Heel to toe on one line is the drill.

faults.label: Leaning on the wall
faults.tip: Hold something for safety, but let the ankles do the balancing.

guide.surface: Firm floor, a line on it if possible.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the heel really touches the toes.

points.t: Heel to toe on one line.
Still and upright.

moves.name: Heel walk & toe walk
moves.summary: Walk a few metres on the heels with toes lifted, then back on the toes with heels lifted.
moves.setup: Walk 5–10 m on the heels, toes pulled up, then return on the balls of the feet, heels high. Small steps, tall posture.
moves.why: Walking toward and away from the phone changes the framing every step; the count and the foot position are not measurable. Follow the guide and log the set.
moves.progression: Longer distance; carry a light weight.
moves.regression: Shorter distance; hand on a wall.
moves.contraindications: Shin or Achilles pain that builds.

faults.label: Toes or heels dropping mid-way
faults.tip: Shorten the walk before the foot drops; the position is the exercise.

faults.label: Leaning to keep balance
faults.tip: Eyes ahead, trunk upright; use small steps rather than leaning.

faults.label: Distance too short
faults.tip: The point is fatigue in the shin and calf. A few steps will not reach it.

faults.label: Bending the knees to cheat
faults.tip: Bending the knees lets the hips lift the foot instead of the shin.

guide.cannotSee: Any of it — the distance to the phone changes every step.

points.t: Toes up on the heel walk; heels high on the toe walk.

moves.name: Lateral hop
equipment: a line or low object to clear
moves.summary: Hop side to side over a line on one leg, landing softly with the knee over the toes.
moves.setup: Stand on one leg beside a line, facing the phone. Hop sideways over the line and stick the landing, knee soft and over the middle of the foot, then hop back.
moves.why: The landing quality is what matters and it happens in a fraction of a second — too fast and too small for the phone to judge honestly. Follow the guide and log the set.
moves.tempo: Stick each landing for a second.
moves.progression: Further apart; faster; over a low object.
moves.contraindications: Any pain on landing; recent sprain not yet cleared for hopping.

faults.label: Knee caving on landing
faults.tip: Land with the knee tracking over the middle of the foot; if it dives inward, hop smaller.

faults.label: Not sticking the landing
faults.tip: The landing is the exercise. If you cannot hold it still for a second, hop smaller.

faults.label: Landing stiff
faults.tip: Bend the knee and hip on landing so it is quiet; a loud landing is a stiff one.

faults.label: Hopping too far too soon
faults.tip: Distance is the last thing to add. Control first, height second, distance last.

guide.surface: Firm, non-slip floor with a line.
guide.cannotSee: The landing — it is over before the phone can judge it.

points.t: Soft, quiet, knee over the middle toes, hips level.
